territorial_scope.description: Michigan state statute enacted by the state legislature; obligations and enforcement are tied to the State of Michigan.

evidence.quote: the people of the state of michigan enact:

summary.short: A bill that would require large developers of foundation models to publish and follow safety and security protocols for critical risks, publish transparency reports, undergo annual third-party audits, and protect employees who report risks, from January 1, 2026, with attorney general civil enforcement.
summary.long: Introduced June 24, 2025 and referred to the Judiciary Committee, the bill would require 'large developers' of foundation models to produce, publish and follow safety and security protocols for critical risks from January 1, 2026. A large developer has developed a foundation model with computing power costing at least $5,000,000 and, within the preceding 12 months, models costing at least $100,000,000 in computing power. Critical risks include death or serious injury to more than 100 people, or over $1,000,000,000 in damages, from incidents such as weapons of mass destruction or cyberattacks. Developers must publish transparency reports at least every 90 days, keep test records for 5 years, and undergo an annual third-party audit published within 90 days. Employees who report critical risks are protected from retaliation. The attorney general may seek fines of up to $1,000,000 per violation of the publication or audit sections, plus injunctive relief; employees may sue for retaliation.

relations.note: Sec. 11 (employee protections) states that it does not invalidate or limit protections under the Whistleblowers' Protection Act. The target is not in the registry, so no instrument ID is given.

notes: The only instrument-level relation is the cross-reference to the Whistleblowers' Protection Act in Sec. 11(9). The text has no legal_basis, amends, repeals, implements or transposes clauses. Internal references to Secs. 5, 7 and 9 are within the bill and are not coded as relations. The annotated text is the bill as introduced on June 24, 2025, with no enactment or amendment history. Sec. 13(1)(a) ($1,000,000 per violation) and Sec. 11(7) ($500) cover different violations and are not inconsistent.

thresholds.variable_text: persons killed or seriously injured in a critical-risk incident
thresholds.measurement: Prospective: the foreseeable and material risk that the large developer's development, storage, or deployment of a foundation model will result in the harm, through an incident of a kind listed in Sec. 3(b)(i) to (iv)
thresholds.consequence: Defines 'critical risk'; the protocol, transparency, audit, and whistleblower provisions refer to critical risks as so defined.
thresholds.conditions: Alternative to the monetary-damages limb in the same definition; the risk must be foreseeable and material.

evidence.quote: will result in the death of, or serious injury to, more than 100 people

thresholds.variable_text: damages to rights in money or property from a critical-risk incident
thresholds.measurement: Prospective: the foreseeable and material risk that the large developer's development, storage, or deployment of a foundation model will result in the damages, through an incident of a kind listed in Sec. 3(b)(i) to (iv)
thresholds.consequence: Defines 'critical risk' by reference to monetary damages; alternative to the death or serious injury limb.
thresholds.conditions: Alternative to the death or serious injury limb in the same definition; the risk must be foreseeable and material.

evidence.quote: will result in more than $1,000,000,000.00 in damages to rights in money or property

thresholds.variable_text: cost of computing power used to develop a foundation model
thresholds.value_text: a quantity of computing power that costs not less than $5,000,000.00
thresholds.measurement: Measured using prevailing market prices of cloud computing in the United States at the time the computing power was used
thresholds.consequence: One of two cumulative limbs that define a large developer, to which the act's duties apply.
thresholds.conditions: Must be met jointly with the limb in Sec. 3(f)(ii) (developer has also developed, within the preceding 12 months, foundation models of the stated computing cost).
